### <a id="connector-id"></a>`connector_id`

The identifier of the meter connector instance that produced the metric.

- **Type:** string
- **Stability:** development
- **Examples:** `0b8f4a6e-2c1d-4e5f-9a7b-3c6d8e1f2a4b`

A UUID assigned when the connector instance is created.

### <a id="signoz-io-workload"></a>`signoz.io/workload`

The SigNoz workload a Kubernetes node is dedicated to.

- **Type:** string
- **Stability:** development
- **Examples:** `clickhouse`

The value of the node's `signoz.io/workload` label.

Known values: `clickhouse`, `redpanda`, `consumers`, `zookeeper`,
`gateway`, `signoz`.

### <a id="signoz-meter-cpu-node-allocatable-usage"></a>`signoz.meter.cpu.node.allocatable.usage`

The amount of CPU allocatable on a Kubernetes node that runs SigNoz.

- **Instrument:** gauge
- **Unit:** `{cpu}`- **Stability:** development
- **Entities:** `k8s.node`

The value is in CPU cores and is recorded once per node every hour.

### <a id="signoz-meter-metric-datapoint-count"></a>`signoz.meter.metric.datapoint.count`

The number of metric data points observed.

- **Instrument:** counter
- **Unit:** `1`- **Stability:** development

A gauge or sum data point counts as one. A histogram data point counts
as its number of buckets plus one for its count and one each for its
sum, min and max when present.
A summary data point counts as its number of quantiles plus two.
Exponential histogram data points, and metrics whose name starts with
`signoz` or `otelcol`, are not counted.

| Attribute | Type | Requirement | Stability | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`connector_id`](#connector-id) | string | Required | development | The identifier of the meter connector instance that produced the metric. |
| [`deployment.environment`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/v1.44.0/docs/registry/attributes/deployment.md#deployment-environment) | string | Recommended | development | OpenTelemetry has renamed this to `deployment.environment.name`; SigNoz uses this name. |
| [`host.name`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/v1.44.0/docs/registry/attributes/host.md#host-name) | string | Recommended | development | Name of the host. On UNIX systems, it may contain what the hostname command returns, or the fully qualified hostname, or another name specified by the user. |
| [`service.name`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/v1.44.0/docs/registry/attributes/service.md#service-name) | string | Recommended | stable | Logical name of the service. |
